passages.text: Then Joseph fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Jacob had just died.
Joseph went to his father.
Joseph fell on his father’s face.
Joseph wept over his father.
Joseph kissed his father.
passages.original: וַיִּפֹּ֥ל יוֹסֵ֖ף עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ עָלָ֖יו וַיִּשַּׁק־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Joseph directed the physicians in his service to embalm his father Israel. So they embalmed him, taking the forty days required to complete the embalming. And the Egyptians mourned for him seventy days.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob, also called Israel.
Joseph served as a leader in Egypt.
Joseph had physicians who worked for him.
Joseph told his physicians to embalm his father Israel.
The physicians embalmed Israel.
The embalming process took forty days.
This was the usual time for embalming.
The Egyptians mourned for Israel.
They mourned for seventy days.
passages.original: וַיְצַ֨ו יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶת־ עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶת־ הָרֹ֣פְאִ֔ים לַחֲנֹ֖ט אֶת־ אָבִ֑יו וַיַּחַנְט֥וּ הָרֹפְאִ֖ים אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וַיִּמְלְאוּ־ לוֹ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יִמְלְא֖וּ יְמֵ֣י הַחֲנֻטִ֑ים וַיִּבְכּ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ מִצְרַ֖יִם שִׁבְעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃

passages.text: When the days of mourning had passed, Joseph said to Pharaoh’s court, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please tell Pharaoh that my father made me swear an oath when he said, ‘I am about to die. You must bury me in the tomb that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.’ Now let me go and bury my father, and then return.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob, also called Israel.
Joseph served as a leader in Egypt.
Joseph mourned for his father after his death.
The days of mourning ended.
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s court.
Joseph said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please speak to Pharaoh for me.”
Joseph explained, “My father made me swear an oath.”
Joseph said, “My father told me, ‘I am about to die.’”
Joseph said, “My father told me, ‘You must bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan.’”
Joseph asked, “Let me go and bury my father.”
Joseph promised, “I will return.”
passages.original: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י בְכִית֔וֹ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶל־ בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־ נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם דַּבְּרוּ־ נָ֕א בְּאָזְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָבִ֞י הִשְׁבִּיעַ֣נִי לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ מֵת֒ בְּקִבְרִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר כָּרִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן שָׁ֖מָּה תִּקְבְּרֵ֑נִי וְעַתָּ֗ה אֶֽעֱלֶה־ נָּ֛א וְאֶקְבְּרָ֥ה אֶת־ אָבִ֖י וְאָשֽׁוּבָה׃

passages.text: Pharaoh replied, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear to do.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, "Go up."
Pharaoh said, "Bury your father."
Pharaoh said, "Do as your father made you swear."
Joseph had promised his father to bury him in Canaan.
Pharaoh gave Joseph permission to keep his promise.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֑ה עֲלֵ֛ה וּקְבֹ֥ר אֶת־ אָבִ֖יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁבִּיעֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Then Joseph went to bury his father, and all the servants of Pharaoh accompanied him—the elders of Pharaoh’s household and all the elders of the land of Egypt— along with all of Joseph’s household, and his brothers, and his father’s household. Only their children and flocks and herds were left in Goshen.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph went to bury his father Jacob.
All the servants of Pharaoh went with Joseph.
The elders of Pharaoh’s household went with him.
All the elders of the land of Egypt went with him.
All of Joseph’s household went with him.
Joseph’s brothers went with him.
Joseph’s father’s household went with him.
They left only their children in Goshen.
They left their flocks in Goshen.
They left their herds in Goshen.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַל יוֹסֵ֖ף לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־ אָבִ֑יו וַיַּֽעֲל֨וּ אִתּ֜וֹ כָּל־ עַבְדֵ֤י פַרְעֹה֙ זִקְנֵ֣י בֵית֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל זִקְנֵ֥י אֶֽרֶץ־ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ וְכֹל֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאֶחָ֖יו וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו רַ֗ק טַפָּם֙ וְצֹאנָ֣ם וּבְקָרָ֔ם עָזְב֖וּ בְּאֶ֥רֶץ גֹּֽשֶׁן׃

passages.text: Chariots and horsemen alike went up with him, and it was an exceedingly large procession.
passages.sermon:
Joseph led the journey to bury his father.
Many people went with Joseph.
Chariots went with Joseph.
Horsemen went with Joseph.
The group was very large.
The procession was impressive.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַל עִמּ֔וֹ גַּם־ רֶ֖כֶב גַּם־ פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כָּבֵ֥ד מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: When they reached the threshing floor of Atad, which is across the Jordan, they lamented and wailed loudly, and Joseph mourned for his father seven days.
passages.sermon:
Joseph led a large group to bury his father Jacob.
They traveled with many people from Egypt.
They reached the threshing floor of Atad.
This place is across the Jordan River.
There, they mourned deeply.
They wailed with great sorrow.
Joseph mourned for his father.
He mourned for seven days.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַד־ גֹּ֣רֶן הָאָטָ֗ד אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיִּ֨סְפְּדוּ־ שָׁ֔ם מִסְפֵּ֛ד גָּד֥וֹל וְכָבֵ֖ד מְאֹ֑ד וַיַּ֧עַשׂ לְאָבִ֛יו אֵ֖בֶל שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: When the Canaanites of the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a solemn ceremony of mourning by the Egyptians.” Thus the place across the Jordan is called Abel-mizraim.
passages.sermon:
The Canaanites lived in the land.
They saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad.
They said, “This is a great mourning for Egypt.”
Because of this, people called the place Abel-mizraim.
This place is across the Jordan.
passages.original: וַיַּ֡רְא יוֹשֵׁב֩ הָאָ֨רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֜י אֶת־ הָאֵ֗בֶל בְּגֹ֙רֶן֙ הָֽאָטָ֔ד וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵֽבֶל־ כָּבֵ֥ד זֶ֖ה לְמִצְרָ֑יִם עַל־ כֵּ֞ן קָרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ אָבֵ֣ל מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

passages.text: So Jacob’s sons did as he had charged them.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of the sons in this story.
Jacob gave his sons instructions before he died.
Jacob’s sons obeyed him.
They did exactly what Jacob told them to do.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ בָנָ֖יו ל֑וֹ כֵּ֖ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּֽם׃

passages.text: They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre, which Abraham had purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
passages.sermon:
Jacob’s sons carried Jacob’s body to the land of Canaan.
They buried Jacob in the cave at Machpelah.
The cave is in a field near Mamre.
Abraham bought this field and cave from Ephron the Hittite.
Abraham purchased it to be a burial site.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ בָנָיו֙ אַ֣רְצָה כְּנַ֔עַן וַיִּקְבְּר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ בִּמְעָרַ֖ת שְׂדֵ֣ה הַמַּכְפֵּלָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָה֩ אַבְרָהָ֨ם אֶת־ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה לַאֲחֻזַּת־ קֶ֗בֶר מֵאֵ֛ת עֶפְרֹ֥ן הַחִתִּ֖י עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י מַמְרֵֽא׃

passages.text: After Joseph had buried his father, he returned to Egypt with his brothers and all who had gone with him to bury his father.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph buried his father Jacob in Canaan.
After the burial, Joseph returned to Egypt.
His brothers returned with him.
All the people who went with Joseph to bury his father also returned to Egypt.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יוֹסֵ֤ף מִצְרַ֙יְמָה֙ ה֣וּא וְאֶחָ֔יו וְכָל־ הָעֹלִ֥ים אִתּ֖וֹ לִקְבֹּ֣ר אֶת־ אָבִ֑יו אַחֲרֵ֖י קָבְר֥וֹ אֶת־ אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph bears a grudge? Then he will surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead.
They became afraid.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “What if Joseph holds a grudge against us?”
They remembered the wrong they had done to Joseph.
They said, “He might repay us for all the evil we did to him.”
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֤וּ אֲחֵֽי־ יוֹסֵף֙ כִּי־ מֵ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ ל֥וּ יִשְׂטְמֵ֖נוּ יוֹסֵ֑ף וְהָשֵׁ֤ב יָשִׁיב֙ לָ֔נוּ אֵ֚ת כָּל־ הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּמַ֖לְנוּ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So they sent word to Joseph, saying, “Before he died, your father commanded, ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.’ So now, Joseph, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” When their message came to him, Joseph wept.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers sent a message to him.
They said, “Your father gave a command before he died.”
He said, “Tell Joseph this.”
“Please forgive your brothers.”
“They sinned against you.”
“They did evil to you.”
“Now, please forgive the servants of the God of your father.”
Joseph heard their message.
Joseph wept.
passages.original: וַיְצַוּ֕וּ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבִ֣יךָ צִוָּ֔ה לִפְנֵ֥י מוֹת֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּֽה־ תֹאמְר֣וּ לְיוֹסֵ֗ף אָ֣נָּ֡א שָׂ֣א נָ֠א פֶּ֣שַׁע אַחֶ֤יךָ וְחַטָּאתָם֙ כִּי־ רָעָ֣ה גְמָל֔וּךָ וְעַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א נָ֔א לְפֶ֥שַׁע עַבְדֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֑יךָ וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ יוֹסֵ֖ף בְּדַבְּרָ֥ם אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: His brothers also came to him, bowed down before him, and said, “We are your slaves!”
passages.sermon: Joseph’s brothers came to him.\r\nThey bowed down before Joseph.\r\nThey said to Joseph, “We are your slaves.”
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ גַּם־ אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ הִנֶּ֥נּֽוּ לְךָ֖ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

passages.text: But Joseph replied, “Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the ruler in Egypt.
Joseph’s brothers feared him.
Joseph spoke to his brothers.
Joseph said, “Do not be afraid.”
Joseph said, “I am not in the place of God.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף אַל־ תִּירָ֑אוּ כִּ֛י הֲתַ֥חַת אֱלֹהִ֖ים אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good, in order to accomplish a day like this—to preserve the lives of many people.
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to his brothers.
Joseph’s brothers had once planned to harm him.
They intended evil against Joseph.
God intended their actions for good.
God used their actions to bring about this day.
God did this to save the lives of many people.
passages.original: וְאַתֶּ֕ם חֲשַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָלַ֖י רָעָ֑ה אֱלֹהִים֙ חֲשָׁבָ֣הּ לְטֹבָ֔ה לְמַ֗עַן עֲשֹׂ֛ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לְהַחֲיֹ֥ת עַם־ רָֽב׃

passages.text: Therefore do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” So Joseph reassured his brothers and spoke kindly to them.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in Egypt with his brothers.
Joseph spoke to his brothers.
Joseph said, “Do not be afraid.”
Joseph said, “I will provide for you.”
Joseph said, “I will provide for your children.”
Joseph comforted his brothers.
Joseph spoke kindly to his brothers.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־ תִּירָ֔אוּ אָנֹכִ֛י אֲכַלְכֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת־ טַפְּכֶ֑ם וַיְנַחֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל־ לִבָּֽם׃

passages.text: Now Joseph and his father’s household remained in Egypt, and Joseph lived to the age of 110.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in Egypt.
Joseph’s father’s household was also in Egypt.
Joseph stayed there with his family.
Joseph lived for 110 years.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יוֹסֵף֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם ה֖וּא וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יו וַיְחִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: He saw Ephraim’s sons to the third generation, and indeed the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph’s knees.
passages.sermon:
Joseph lived in Egypt.
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph saw the children of Ephraim.
He saw Ephraim’s descendants to the third generation.
Joseph also saw the sons of Machir.
Machir was the son of Manasseh.
The sons of Machir were born during Joseph’s lifetime.
Joseph cared for the sons of Machir.
The sons of Machir grew up on Joseph’s knees.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤רְא יוֹסֵף֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם בְּנֵ֖י שִׁלֵּשִׁ֑ים גַּ֗ם בְּנֵ֤י מָכִיר֙ בֶּן־ מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה יֻלְּד֖וּ עַל־ בִּרְכֵּ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃

passages.text: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land He promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a leader in Egypt.
Joseph spoke to his brothers.
Joseph said, “I am about to die.
God will surely visit you.
God will bring you up from this land.
God promised this land to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God swore this promise to them.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־ אֶחָ֔יו אָנֹכִ֖י מֵ֑ת וֵֽאלֹהִ֞ים פָּקֹ֧ד יִפְקֹ֣ד אֶתְכֶ֗ם וְהֶעֱלָ֤ה אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את אֶל־ הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֛ע לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: And Joseph made the sons of Israel take an oath and said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones up from this place.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a leader among the sons of Israel.
Joseph spoke to the sons of Israel.
Joseph made the sons of Israel take an oath.
Joseph said, “God will surely attend to you.”
Joseph said, “You must carry my bones up from this place.”
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע יוֹסֵ֔ף אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר פָּקֹ֨ד יִפְקֹ֤ד אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְהַעֲלִתֶ֥ם אֶת־ עַצְמֹתַ֖י מִזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So Joseph died at the age of 110. And they embalmed his body and placed it in a coffin in Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a leader in Egypt.
Joseph lived to be 110 years old.
Joseph died.
People embalmed Joseph’s body.
They put Joseph’s body in a coffin.
They placed the coffin in Egypt.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣מָת יוֹסֵ֔ף בֶּן־ מֵאָ֥ה וָעֶ֖שֶׂר שָׁנִ֑ים וַיַּחַנְט֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַיִּ֥ישֶׂם בָּאָר֖וֹן בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃
